removed_lines: parish newsletter 25th october 2026 thirtieth sunday in ordinary time no: 2067 mt 22:34-40 “i’m not religious, but i pray pope leo lives for many more years.” so wrote former bbc foreign correspondent, fergal keane, in a recent piece in the sunday independent.
speaking of pope leo he wrote: “witness his condemnation of leaders who twist the truth and disregard the law.

in his address at unesco in paris last month, he said: “instead of respecting the law, those in power invoke it when it serves their interests and disregard it when it restrains them, treating even justice itself as though it were a commodity to be bought and sold.” because he defends migrants and speaks out against wars of aggression, leo has attracted the disapproval of such moral luminaries as america’s vice-president, jd vance, a catholic of a very different colour.

how badly we need a voice like leo’s, a man unafraid of autocrats precisely because he has lived by the principles of justice: as a missionary in peru he bore witness alongside the poor in years of terrible repression and revolutionary violence.

you don’t need to be religious to respect such a man, or to pray that he lives for many more years.” we continue to keep pope leo in our prayers that god will grant him the strength to lead our church and be a messenger of gospel peace and hope for many years to come.
we were glad to learn last wednesday that he needs no further treatment.
